specFirst: This file describes the REAL flow that runs today (aligned 2026-07-11 as step 1 of todo/modernizeChangeBackend.md). Going forward it is the implementation contract, like agentNewSolution3/flow.json: maintenance changes THIS spec first, then the code. The runtime ordering is still IMPERATIVE (each agent's afterPromptStep calls cbShared.enqueueNext with the successor planId); this file's `dependsOn` mirrors that chain and MUST be kept in sync until/if the ordering is derived from `dependsOn` (see modernization.orderingSource).
description: Stage 3 backend reconciler for projects generated by agentNewSolution3. V1 is AUTONOMOUS and CREATE-ONLY: with no user prompt, it scans l5/{module}/todoBackend.defs.ts for owners with status = toCreate, derives the 3-layer HEXAGONAL backend, generates the .defs.ts, materializes them to .ts, generates deterministic seeds.ts, then optionally persists requested image seed assets in L3 before marking the todo owners done. Image failures are warnings and make their seed field null. If there is nothing to create, it finishes immediately without changing files or statuses. Independent of todoFrontend (agentChangeFrontend). See spec.md in this folder. NOTE (2026-07-11): the 4 LLM index steps (aggregate/persistence/usecase/bff) were REMOVED — their output was never persisted and the generators re-derive aggregates/columns/usecases deterministically from the l4/l5 scan; the flow now goes cb-lock -> cb-gen-domain directly.

entry.noInputPolicy: No user prompt. The agent receives no module/owner/item arguments; it discovers all actionable work from l5/{module}/todoBackend.defs.ts. (A single-item arg is an optional future convenience, not required.)
entry.noWorkBehavior: If no owner with todoBackend status = toCreate is found, finish without changing any file or status.

source.tree: _102021_/l2/agentChangeBackend/agentChangeBackend.ts + per-agent enqueueNext/dispatch (IMPERATIVE sequential chain; NOT a declarative planned tree). Two parallel_dynamic fan-outs: cb-usecase-fanout and cb-materialize (one layer per dispatch). The former LLM index chain (cb-lock -> aggregate -> persistence -> usecase -> bff -> gen-domain) was collapsed to cb-lock -> gen-domain on 2026-07-11.
source.schemas: _102021_/l2/agentChangeBackend/helpers/cbSchemas.ts (strict JSON schemas; collab-llm enforces the tool call, cbExtract re-validates).

v1: Run autonomously with no user prompt; discover work from l5/{module}/todoBackend.defs.ts.
Process ONLY owners with todoBackend status = toCreate (new). Exit cleanly when there is no create work.
Derive aggregates from ontology kind + relationships; apply the JSONB model (indexed columns out, the rest + child collections in details).

Generate the 3-layer hexagonal .defs.ts (domain, application, adapters), materialize them to .ts via the reused L1 pipeline, and generate seeds.ts for persistence test data. Optional SeedAssetRef images are generated in L3 after the plan; failures are non-blocking and resolve to null.
Register the persistence manifest, the http router and the port->adapter composition root; fix l0/config.json backend entrypoints.
Mark processed owners todoBackend status = done after their artifacts + .ts validate.
Use JSON-schema-backed tool output whenever an LLM is used (local cbPlanner/cbSchemas pattern).
explicitlyNotInV1: No user-provided module/owner/item filters (pure autonomous scan).
No clarification / no blocking human input.
No processing of toUpdate / toRemove / inProgress / done owners.
deferredToV2: toUpdate diff and preservation of manual edits.
toRemove cascade (deprecate table/impl, drop with confirmation, data safety).
Patching artifacts created by a previous run.

repairLoopAndJudge._note: Implemented 2026-07-04 (was deferredToV2 'Critic/repair LLM loop'). Shared block with ns2 (todo/ajustesFinaisChangeBackend.md §2 + improveAddNewSolution2_1.md §4.3/§4.4). The flow ENGINE is untouched: 'reopening' a step = enqueueing a fresh step with a unique planId/args; durable routing state lives in l4/trace/cb-repair-state.json (cbRepair.ts).
repairLoopAndJudge.componentRepair: agentCbMaterialize worker failures (validator findings, missing tool code, AND per-file TypeScript compile errors — spec item 11) are recorded with the findings + rejected code; the dispatcher re-spawns the worker (unique planId cb-mat-L{rank}[-g{round}][-r{attempt}]) with the findings injected into the prompt. A saved-but-not-compiling .ts is forced stale again so the re-spawn happens and cb-validate-all's staleness check blocks whatever never converges. Budget: 2 repairs per component (3 LLM calls). No console output on repair paths: the trace lands on the step, the audit in cb-repair-state.history, and cb-validate-all embeds the history in the task trace.
repairLoopAndJudge.judge: agentCbJudge (cb-judge) runs right after cb-usecase-fanout — the first durable LLM artifact consumed downstream — and BEFORE controllers/materialization. Adversarial critic (LLM validates, never generates): usecase defs vs L4 contract (ports, rulesApplied, inputs vs accessPattern, contextResolution, acceptanceAssertions). Findings typed by the taxonomy estrutural|decisao|fora_de_escopo; fora_de_escopo discarded. Error findings re-spawn the origin agentCbUsecase workers with findings in context, then cb-judge-r2 re-verifies SCOPED to the repaired owners only (args.owners — mechanical, cheaper); leftovers are downgraded to warnings — the judge signals, the deterministic gates keep blocking.
repairLoopAndJudge.globalRepair: agentCbValidateAll failure with ALL findings materialization-level (bad/missing .ts) triggers ONE repair round: force the component defs stale + record findings + re-enqueue cb-materialize in repair mode (skips seeds/register — defs unchanged) -> cb-validate-all-g{n}. Defs-level findings or exhausted budget -> CLEAN failure with the objective trace (never soften the gate).
repairLoopAndJudge.engineSemantics: LESSON (run 2026-07-04, task1): a FAILED step does NOT satisfy dependsOn — a failed parallel child fails its parent and the joined step (continue-dispatcher / cb-judge) waits forever, killing the task with no repair and no report. Therefore WORKER children NEVER return 'failed': failures complete with a '[repair]'/'[worker-error]' trace + a cb-repair-state record; the dispatcher re-spawns what has budget and cb-validate-all (sequential) is the step that actually fails the run — cleanly, with the objective findings.

notResponsible: horizontalOwned tables (owned by the horizontal module, e.g. Payment).
Pages / screens / menu, per-page contract authoring, frontend client functions (statusFrontend / agentChangeFrontend).
Authoring ontology / operations / workflows / rules (consumed only).

conventions.selfContained: Everything lives in l2/agentChangeBackend/. The only cross-folder reuse is the L1 materialization in l2/agentMaterializeSolution/.
conventions.agentNaming: Root + focused agents: agentCb* (clean single-purpose prompts). Materialization agents are REUSED by their existing names (agentPrepareDefsL1, agentMaterializeL1Def, agentMaterializeGen).
conventions.toolCallJsonSchema: Every LLM step returns its result through ONE tool call validated against a strict JSON schema (helpers/cbPlanner.ts + helpers/cbSchemas.ts pattern, plus the existing submitL1Pipeline tool). collab-llm enforces the schema; cbExtract re-validates before saving. No free-form prose results.
conventions.inputLayer: Reads l4 (BUSINESS, frozen by Stage 1): l4/{module}/module.defs.ts (ontology index + relationships), l4/{module}/ontology/*.defs.ts (canonical entity kind/fields), l4/operations/*.defs.ts, l4/workflows/*.defs.ts, l4/rules/*.defs.ts. The page bffCommands + per-page contract (l2/{module}/web/contracts/{page}.defs.ts) are CONSUMED when present (produced by agentChangeFrontend). Writes l1/{module} (3 hexagonal layers).
conventions.hexagonalLayers: layer_1_external/adapters (http: routes + controllers = BFF; persistence: repositories + TableDefinition; queues/webhooks/cron/plugins) ; layer_2_application (usecases/services/ports/dto/commands/queries) ; layer_3_domain (entities/value-objects/domain-services/rules/events). Dependency points INWARD; ctx.data ONLY inside adapters/persistence.
conventions.aggregateDerivation: From ontology kind + relationships: core -> 1 physical table + domain aggregate root + repository port + repository adapter ; supporting (oneToMany/oneToOne under a core, no direct query) -> EMBEDDED in the root details JSONB as a value-object (NO own table) ; event (append-only) -> own table ; mdm -> NO table (read-only via 102034 shared MDM runtime).
conventions.jsonbModel: Maximize JSONB. Real columns ONLY for fields that need an index (PK, queried FKs, status/lifecycle, ordering/filter timestamps used by operations/workflows). Everything else + supporting child collections -> single details JSONB column (e.g. Order.details.items: OrderItem[]). Promote a details field to a column only when it becomes filtered/indexed.
conventions.mdmPersistence: MDM table persistence is EXCLUSIVELY 102034 (mdm_documents, mdm_documents_entities_index, ...). This flow NEVER emits an MDM TableDefinition and NEVER registers an MDM table in the manifest; it only reads via the shared MDM runtime. horizontalOwned follows the same principle.
conventions.namingDeterminism: All code identifiers derive deterministically from the canonical ontology entityId / operationId (Order -> domain Order, table order/orders, port OrderRepository, usecase createOrder). The PT title ('Pedido') is a UI label ONLY — never a file/class/column name. (Fixes the legacy Order -> pedidoEntity drift.)

ownerStatus.failureStatus: leave as inProgress and write a trace record; v1 has no failed enum
ownerStatus.independentOf: statusFrontend (agentChangeFrontend) — no mandatory order between the two reconcilers

layerKnowledge.problem: The BFF must know the application (layer_2) functions; the application must know the domain; and persistence must serve the domain — but the DOMAIN must not know persistence. How is the chain wired?
layerKnowledge.compileTime: Resolved by the materialization dependsFiles (.d.ts) chain, generated INNER-FIRST: domain (imports nothing) -> repository port + table (import domain) -> usecase (imports domain + port) -> repository adapter (imports port + domain + table) -> http controller (imports the usecase function/types + the per-page contract Output). Each artifact's pipeline lists EXACTLY the inner-layer .d.ts it imports, so agentMaterializeGen always has the callee's signatures as context.
layerKnowledge.runtime: Dependency Inversion. The usecase depends ONLY on the repository PORT interface (layer_2_application/ports), NEVER on the concrete adapter. register-backend builds the composition root that binds each port -> its adapter; usecases resolve repositories from ctx by port (same registry pattern as ctx.data.moduleData.getTable today). So persistence depends on the domain/port — not the reverse.
layerKnowledge.correction: There is NO domain->persistence dependency. The arrow is INVERTED: persistence (adapter) implements a port owned by the application, and imports the domain; the domain is the innermost ring and imports nothing. BFF->application and application->domain are normal inward imports; application<->persistence is inverted through the port.

conventions.defsSelfSufficiency: Each generated .defs.ts MUST be SUFFICIENT to generate its .ts: agentMaterializeGen (a separate agent) consumes ONLY the .defs.ts, nothing else. So every .defs.ts carries (a) the complete `data` planning block (the WHAT) and (b) `export const pipeline` = one item with everything the LLM needs: outputPath (.ts), defPath, dependsFiles[] (.d.ts signatures of the inner callee layer), dependsOn[], skills[] = the LLM CONTEXT (layer skill _102021_/l2/skills/layer_*.md + platform _102034_.d.ts), rulesPath?+rulesApplied? (authoritative rule text), afterSaveBackEnd? (deterministic register hook), agent='agentMaterializeGen'. If the LLM would need anything not in `data` nor reachable via dependsFiles/skills/rulesPath, the .defs.ts is incomplete. Canonical example: _102043_/l1/cafeFlow/layer_1_external/dailySalesMetrics.defs.ts.
conventions.materialization: Reuses the L1 pipeline: gen-* writes the `data` block; agentPrepareDefsL1 appends `export const pipeline` to each .defs.ts in dependency order; agentMaterializeL1Def resolves outputPath + dependsFiles + attaches skills/rulesPath per item via tool call; agentMaterializeGen generates the .ts from the self-sufficient .defs.ts. Then deterministic registrars wire the manifest, the router and the composition root.
conventions.fanOutReads: Parallel fan-out children are pre-allocated, reused and DELETED after completion. Consumers that run AFTER a fan-out read the SAVED .defs.ts files (file-fallback), never task payloads.
conventions.verification: Deterministic, NON-blocking preflight (cb-validate-readiness) checks entity/operation refs resolve against canonical l4 ids (unresolved -> warnings); the final validate (cb-validate-all) reads the SAVED l1 files (ctx.data only in adapters/persistence; no MDM table; contract shape honored).
conventions.modelPolicy: No LLM for deterministic scan, status mutation, registration and validation — NOR for aggregate/column/usecase planning (that is now derived deterministically from the scan; the LLM index steps were removed 2026-07-11). When an LLM is required, force strict JSON-schema tool output. Use modelType code for backend defs, usecase workers, technical judging and final .ts materialization; use modelType image only for optional seed asset generation.

modernization._note: Target of todo/modernizeChangeBackend.md: migrate this flat folder (agents + infra) to the agentNewSolution3 pattern (1 folder per maintenance unit under steps/), prompts in .md, a minimal policy-frozen shared core, and this flow.json as the spec-first contract. External behavior (generated artifacts, /run|/rebuild CLI, l4/l5 contract) stays identical.
modernization.orderingSource: IMPERATIVE today: each agent's afterPromptStep calls cbShared.enqueueNext(successorPlanId). `dependsOn` here MIRRORS that chain and is kept in sync by hand. Candidate future change (like ns3 done-anchors): derive ordering from `dependsOn`. Until then, the successor of each step is declared in ONE place (that step's agent), never duplicated across files.
modernization.indexStepsCut: 2026-07-11: cb-aggregate-index, cb-persistence-index, cb-usecase-index, cb-bff-index (agentCbAggregateIndex/PersistenceIndex/UsecaseIndex/BffIndex) + their schemas were removed. They called the LLM with a strict schema but the output was NEVER persisted; the downstream generators re-derive aggregates (cbShared.deriveAggregates), indexed columns (cbShared.planTableColumns) and usecases deterministically from the l4/l5 scan. Removing them keeps the generated artifacts identical while cutting 4 LLM calls (cost + latency + noise).

folderLayout._note: APPLIED 2026-07-11 (todo/modernizeChangeBackend.md §Ordem 4): each step agent now lives under steps/<slug>/ with its prompt.md, readme.md and CHANGELOG.md. Agents are resolved by agentName (getInstanceByName scans the project), so the move needed no import changes — only fileReference + agentFolder updates. The shared core stays flat (see sharedCoreFrozen).
folderLayout.steps/scan/: cb-scan (agentCbScanCreateOwners) + cb-validate-readiness (agentCbValidateL4Readiness) + cb-lock (agentCbLockOwners) — deterministic input steps, small, always edited together.
folderLayout.steps/gen-usecase/: cb-gen-usecase dispatcher + cb-usecase-fanout worker + repair integration, in separate files; the worker prompt (largest of the project) in its own prompt.md.
folderLayout.steps/judge/: cb-judge (agentCbJudge) — adversarial critic + finding routing to repair.
folderLayout.steps/materialize/: cb-materialize dispatcher (layer barrier) + cb-mat-L{rank} worker + component validators + repair hints. Densest folder; readme must document the '1 layer per dispatch' barrier.
folderLayout.steps/gen-seed-assets/: cb-seed-assets (agentCbSeedAssets): optional image requests, WebP conversion, L3 asset persistence and seed-assets.json manifest. This step owns the asset boundary; a failure is a warning and leaves the seed URL null.
folderLayout.steps/validate-all/: cb-validate-all (agentCbValidateAll) — global validation barrier + global repair.
folderLayout.helpers/: Shared, cross-step and policy-frozen helpers: cbShared (to be split by responsibility), cbSchemas, component validators, cbMaterializeCore, cbMaterializeIo, cbRepair, cbMdmGuards and cbSeedsCore. cbMaterializeCore is the FROZEN boundary shared with the CLI (nodejsMaterializeL1) and the harness (tools/materializeHarness.mjs) — touch it and you review all 3 consumers.
folderLayout.skillsCentralized: skills/*.md (per-layer materialization context) stay centralized — consumed by materialize AND the CLI, not owned by one step.

engineInvariants._note: collab-messages engine rules that were living in code comments. They are the biggest source of silent regression; keep them here as an explicit contract and enforce in gates/tests when steps move to folders.
engineInvariants.workerNeverFailed: A parallel fan-out WORKER child (cb-usecase-fanout, cb-mat-L{rank}) NEVER returns 'failed': a failed child fails its parent and the joined step (dispatcher / cb-judge / cb-validate-all) waits forever, killing the task with no repair and no report. On failure the worker COMPLETES with a '[repair]'/'[worker-error]' trace + a cb-repair-state record; the sequential barrier step (cb-validate-all) is the only place that fails the run, cleanly, with objective findings.
engineInvariants.layerBarrier: Materialization is ONE LAYER PER DISPATCH. The runtime's addParallelArgs forces a parallel parent to in_progress at creation, so creating all layers at once is NOT a barrier (real bug: controllers materialized while usecases were 13/18). cb-materialize spawns only the innermost stale layer (cb-mat-L{rank}) plus a sequential continue-dispatcher (cb-mat-after-L{rank}) that waits on that layer and re-runs the dispatch.
engineInvariants.planIdUniqueness: 'Reopening' a step = enqueueing a FRESH step with a UNIQUE planId/args (repairs and adjustment runs have dynamic planIds — see dynamicPlanIds). unlockWaitingDependencySteps only unlocks on a COMPLETED step per planId, so downstream must depend on stable anchors, never on a run's dynamic planId.
engineInvariants.addChildBeforeCompletingParent: In a fan-out, add the NEXT child (or the join/continue-dispatcher) BEFORE completing the current step; collab-messages auto-completes a parent once its children are done, so completing first orphans the successor.

dynamicPlanIds._note: Runtime-generated planIds (not static flow steps). Documented so the barrier/repair logic is auditable.
dynamicPlanIds.cb-usecase-repair-r{n}: Judge re-spawn of the origin usecase workers with findings injected; cb-judge-r{n+1} re-verifies scoped to the repaired owners (max judgeRuns=2).
dynamicPlanIds.cb-mat-L{rank}[-g{round}][-r{attempt}]: Materialization worker per layer rank; -g{round} = validate-all global repair round; -r{attempt} = component repair attempt (max componentRepairs=2).
dynamicPlanIds.cb-mat-after-L{rank}[-g{round}]: Sequential continue-dispatcher that waits on layer {rank} and re-runs cb-materialize for the next stale layer (the real barrier).
dynamicPlanIds.cb-validate-all-g{n}: cb-validate-all re-run after a global materialization repair round (globalRounds=1; seeds/register stay valid because defs are unchanged).
dynamicPlanIds.cb-judge-r{n}: Scoped judge re-verification pass over repaired owners.
dynamicPlanIds.repairState: l4/trace/cb-repair-state.json (cbRepair.ts) is the durable routing state shared by judge, materialize dispatcher, worker and validate-all — the explicit cross-step boundary when steps move into folders.

modelAliases._note: Model type preferences. Stored here so the flow is self-describing; each LLM step picks one via its `modelAlias` field. modelType hints inside prompts (e.g. <!-- modelType: code -->) must match the chosen alias.

reads: l2/{module}/web/contracts/{page}.defs.ts (per-page contract, when frontend already ran)
writes: l5/{module}/todoBackend.defs.ts status for processed operation/workflow owners
explicitlyNotWritten: horizontalOwned tables (owned by the horizontal module)
Pages / screens / menu / per-page contract / frontend client functions (statusFrontend)
ontology / operations / workflows / rules (consumed, never authored)

steps.goal: Root orchestrator. No input args. Reads the CLI command (run|rebuild-defs|rebuild-all) and enqueues cb-scan. Finishes immediately if the scan finds no toCreate work.
DETERMINISTIC. Read l4/l5 and select owners (operations/workflows) with todoBackend status = toCreate. Enqueue cb-validate-readiness.
DETERMINISTIC preflight: entity/operation refs resolve to canonical l4 ids; non-blocking warnings. Enqueue cb-lock.

DETERMINISTIC. Set todoBackend status = inProgress for the selected owners (operations AND workflows). Enqueue cb-gen-domain (the LLM index steps were removed 2026-07-11; aggregates/columns/usecases are derived deterministically by the generators).

LLM, WHOLE LAYER in one call (array result). Pure domain entities per aggregate root + value-objects, plus one immutable record per persisted event. Aggregates are derived deterministically (cbShared.deriveAggregates) from ontology kind + relationships. Enqueue cb-gen-port.
LLM, whole layer. Repository ports I{Entity}Repository per aggregate; append-only ports (append+finders) per persisted event. Enqueue cb-gen-table.
LLM, whole layer. TableDefinition per core root + per persisted event (append-only, purpose 'controle', retentionDays). MDM/reaction produce NO table. Enqueue cb-gen-adapter.
LLM, whole layer. Repository adapters implementing the ports (domain<->row + details JSONB; MDM via 102034; event adapters do insert-only). Enqueue cb-gen-usecase.
DISPATCHER (no LLM). Fan out one usecase worker per OPERATION owner (cb-usecase-fanout) and enqueue the JUDGE join (cb-judge, waiting_dependency on the fan-out).

LLM WORKER per operation owner: one usecase file with explicit functions[] input/output, orchestrating domain + ports, appending its eventWrites in the same transaction. On a repair re-spawn (judge findings in cb-repair-state) the findings are injected into the prompt. Progress: 'Gerar usecases {{completed}}/{{total}}, falhas {{failed}}'.

JUDGE (adversarial critic, EARLY — before controllers/materialization). LLM VALIDATES, never generates: each usecase defs vs its L4 owner contract (ports, rulesApplied executable, inputs vs accessPattern, contextResolution not turned into manual input, acceptanceAssertions satisfiable) + deterministic missing-defs detection. Error findings -> re-spawn the origin workers (cb-usecase-repair-r{n}) with findings in context, then cb-judge-r{n+1} re-verifies (max 2 passes). Leftover errors on the final pass are DOWNGRADED to warnings (the judge signals; deterministic gates keep blocking). Enqueue cb-gen-http.

DETERMINISTIC (no LLM). V1 module (no workspaces): one controller .defs.ts per OPERATION + boundary DTO .ts. V2 module (has workspaces): one controller .defs.ts per WORKSPACE (page) with N handlers/routes (one per bffCall) carrying usecaseRefs + inputContract + the projection spec (pick/rename/$items) + workspace actors/scopes; the pipeline dependsFiles reference the usecase .d.ts + the l4/contracts/*.defs.ts (context only). BOTH v1 and v2 controllers materialize via cb-materialize (LLM + httpController.md) — the LLM adds auth/filters/adjustments beyond the mechanical projection (user decision 19/jul). The v2 controller imports the USECASE types and projects the wire output structurally — there is NO l1 contract file (the wire contract of record stays in l4; only the FE copies it). Controller .defs.ts are emitted in defs-only too (review artifact). Enqueue cb-materialize — EXCEPT under /rebuild defs (defs-only TOTAL, B2): nothing is materialized and the next step is cb-rebuild-defs-cleanup.

dependsOn: cb-gen-http (ONLY on the /rebuild defs path; never reached in /rebuild all or /run)
steps.goal: DETERMINISTIC (no LLM), /rebuild defs ONLY. Soft-deletes the DERIVED l1 backend .ts (every level-1 non-.defs.ts under the run's modules: domain/port/adapter/table/usecase/controller + seeds.ts + registerRepositories.ts + l1 contract mirror .ts/.d.ts), keeping ONLY the .defs.ts source of truth. Closes the 'stale .ts masks a worker bug' class (runs c-h) and guarantees the next /rebuild all re-materializes from zero. Best-effort: a failure never fails the tree (defs are already regenerated; .ts are recoverable + re-materializable). Enqueue cb-finalize. Trace: 'rebuild-defs: 0 materializados, M .ts soft-deletados'.

DISPATCHER (no LLM), ONE LAYER PER DISPATCH. Spawns only the innermost stale layer (cb-mat-L{rank}) and a sequential continue-dispatcher (cb-mat-after-L{rank}) that waits on that layer's planId and re-runs this dispatch. This is a REAL barrier: the runtime's addParallelArgs forces a parallel parent to in_progress at creation, so creating all layers at once is NOT a barrier (bug: controllers materialized while usecases were 13/18). dispatch is idempotent (materialized .ts stop being stale). REPAIR: a stale entry below minRank whose worker failed WITH budget left (cb-repair-state) is re-included under a unique planId (cb-mat-L{rank}[-g{round}][-r{attempt}]) with the findings injected into the worker prompt; budget exhausted -> skipped (cb-validate-all reports it). Enqueue cb-gen-seeds when all stale layers are done (or cb-validate-all-g{n} in a validate-all repair round, where seeds/register are still valid).

dependsOn: cb-materialize (spawned one rank at a time; each next layer waits on the previous via cb-mat-after-L{rank})
steps.goal: LLM WORKER per .defs.ts of the current layer: generate the final .ts from the self-sufficient defs + dependsFiles (.d.ts) + skill. Layers in order: entidades de domínio(0) -> ports(1) -> tabelas(2) -> adapters(3) -> usecases(4) -> controllers(5). Progress: 'Materializar {layer} {{completed}}/{{total}}, falhas {{failed}}'.

dependsOn: the last cb-mat layer (materialize path only; NOT reached under /rebuild defs — that path ends at cb-rebuild-defs-cleanup)
steps.goal: HYBRID. An LLM returns only a strict JSON scenario plan from L4/L5/table defs; agentCbSeeds validates it deterministically, resolves symbolic refs to stable IDs, and writes l1/{module}/layer_1_external/adapters/persistence/seeds.ts. The plan is embedded and reused when still valid. Generate local, MDM entity/document, and MDM relationship rows; labels use the first language from l5/project.json. A SeedAssetRef is allowed only in declared image/URL fields. Bounded repair (2 attempts) follows validation findings. NON-FATAL: if a wave still won't validate after the repair budget, agentCbSeeds does NOT fail the task (seeds are TEST DATA — the composition root/config/finalize downstream matter more): it FINALIZES with the PARTIAL plan (tablePlans narrowed to the seeded tables so coverage passes; the skipped table is seeded EMPTY) and continues to cb-seed-assets -> cb-register, surfacing the give-up as a WARNING. Then enqueue cb-seed-assets.

OPTIONAL and NON-BLOCKING. For each SeedAssetRef, request an image through responseType:image, convert the temporary PNG to bounded WebP, and write l3/{module}/assets/seed/{EntityId}/{seedKey}.webp plus l3/{module}/assets/seed-assets.json. Reuse only a ready manifest entry whose promptHash and blob remain valid. Failed images are recorded as warnings and resolve to null in seeds.ts; never use external URLs or base64. Enqueue cb-register.

DETERMINISTIC (no LLM). Write the module's backend block into the CLIENT-owned l5/project.json (backendControllers dir + persistence.tableDefsDir + routeKeys) so the final backend step can merge l5/config.json without the masters importing the client (dependency inversion). Guarded: project config failure never aborts. Enqueue cb-validate-all.

DETERMINISTIC barrier. Integrity from the SAVED l1 files: (a) every usecase port has a port + domain entity defs; (b) V1 every controller handler.usecaseRef exists as a usecase export (orderFlow break); V2 (module has workspaces) COHERENCE controller x workspace: every bffCall has an exported handler registered in routes by its route const (rotas esperadas = bffCalls do workspace, not per-operation bffName) + the workspace controller .ts compiles; (c) COMPLETENESS: every .defs.ts has its materialized .ts (fails if materialization is incomplete — the project-level check the per-file Monaco compile misses); (d) ORPHANS: every generated .ts must have its .defs.ts, EXCEPT the declared expectedGeneratedTsWithoutDefs below (artifacts compiled deterministically outside the defs->materialize pipeline). REPAIR ROUTING: when EVERY finding is materialization-level (bad/missing .ts) and the global budget (1 round) is available, forces the components stale + records the findings and re-enqueues cb-materialize in repair mode (-> cb-validate-all-g{n}); defs-level findings (incl. V2 controller findings — the deterministic emitter, not materialize, owns them) or exhausted budget FAIL CLEAN, so finalize cannot mark owners done prematurely. Enqueue cb-finalize when clean (clears cb-repair-state).
expectedGeneratedTsWithoutDefs: l1/{module}/layer_1_external/adapters/persistence/seeds.ts (agentCbSeeds compiles it deterministically via cbSeedsCore/saveGeneratedTs; there is no seeds.defs.ts by design — lesson run 2026-07-15 cafeFlow: the orphan check must not block it)

failurePolicy.beforeLock: Fail without changing l4 owner statuses.
failurePolicy.afterLock: Do not mark done. Keep affected owners in inProgress and write trace details (no failed enum in v1).
failurePolicy.partialFailure: A failed artifact blocks done only for the owners that depend on it; unrelated owners may finish.
failurePolicy.noWork: No selected owners means no status or file writes.
failurePolicy.manualRecovery: A later recovery tool or v2 may reset stale inProgress owners to toCreate after inspection.
